CweFindings.Name: Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime
CweFindings.Description: The product does not release a resource after its effective lifetime has ended, i.e., after the resource is no longer needed.
CweFindings.Explanation: PhotoService.UploadPhotoAsync opens an additional stream with file.OpenReadStream() and only sets its Position (line 132); the returned Stream is not assigned to a using scope or disposed after use. Repeated uploads can therefore retain stream resources beyond their effective lifetime.

CweFindings.Name: Missing Synchronization
CweFindings.Description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner but does not attempt to synchronize access to the shared resource.
CweFindings.Explanation: PhotoFileModel.OnGetAsync reads a stored photo while PhotoService.DeletePhotoAsync may delete that same file concurrently. The per-request scoped service does not coordinate these accesses, so concurrent requests can race and make an in-progress photo read fail or observe inconsistent file/database state.

CweFindings.Name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
CweFindings.Description: The product allows the upload or transfer of dangerous file types that are automatically processed within its environment.
CweFindings.Explanation: PhotoService.UploadPhotoAsync trusts the client-provided ContentType when checking the allowlist (lines 82-88), then derives the stored extension from the client-provided filename (line 110). ImageSharp decode failures are caught and ignored (lines 125-138), after which the original bytes are still written to the publicly served uploads directory (lines 140-145). A client can therefore label non-image content with an allowed image MIME type and have it stored and served using its supplied extension.
